section: Science · Light, Heat, Sound, Electricity & Magnetism
subject: Science
stem: Holding one end of a metal spoon in a hot cup of tea, you feel the other end getting warm too, even though it isn't touching the tea directly. Heat travelling through the solid metal like this is called:
explanation: Conduction is heat transfer through direct contact within a solid, typically fastest in metals — distinct from convection (fluid movement) and radiation (electromagnetic waves, no medium needed).

section: Science · Light, Heat, Sound, Electricity & Magnetism
subject: Science
stem: When water is heated in a pot, the hot water at the bottom rises while cooler water sinks to take its place, creating a circulating current that gradually heats the whole pot. This mode of heat transfer through the movement of a fluid is called:
explanation: Convection transfers heat through the actual movement of a fluid as warmer, less dense regions rise and cooler, denser regions sink.

section: Science · Light, Heat, Sound, Electricity & Magnetism
subject: Science
stem: The Sun's heat reaches Earth across the vacuum of space, where there is no matter to conduct or convect heat. This mode of heat transfer, which requires no medium at all, is called:
explanation: Radiation transfers heat via electromagnetic waves and needs no medium — the only way heat crosses the vacuum of space.
